newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money climbs to 3.10/3.15 percent.
newsitem.headline: German call money climbs to 3.10/3.15 percent.

text.p: German call money rates firmed to 3.10/3.15 percent on Monday from about 3.10 percent last Friday, with some traders saying the market could rise as high as 3.20 percent in the near-term, traders said.

The primary reason for higher rates was due to a modest drop in the monthly average of funds held in reserve by banks at the Bundesbank, some traders said. But others were mystified by the higher rates, saying the reasons were not very clear.
"It's hard to understand where the demand for funds is coming from," said one Frankfurt trader.

Some traders said rates may ease after Wednesdays's weekly Bundesbank repo securities allotment at a fixed three percent, which was announced on Monday instead of the regular time on Tuesday due to regional holidays on that day.
The monthly reserve average as of Monday fell to 40.0 billion marks from 41.5 billion marks on Friday, while total reserves dipped slightly to 37.02 billion from 37.1 billion.
Lombard borrowings were steady at about 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= on Monday was trading at about 3.14867 percent compared with 3.13300 percent on Friday.
